summary: Baileys fork hides a predictable default WhatsApp pairing code behind AES-obfuscated literal
details: This package is a fork of the Baileys WhatsApp library in which lib/Socket/socket.js replaces the standard random pairing code with a hardcoded default. The default value is produced at runtime by CryptoJS AES-decrypting the embedded ciphertext `U2FsdGVkX1+LgFmBqo3Wg0zTlHXoebkTRtjmU0cq9Fs=` with the password `ERROR_FILE`, and is bound as the default argument of `requestPairingCode(a, b=Z)`. Any caller that invokes `requestPairingCode` without explicitly supplying a code gets this attacker-known value, which is then fed to `derivePairingCodeKey` to derive the AES-CTR key that encrypts the companion-device registration ephemeral public key sent to WhatsApp during linking. A party holding the plaintext can derive the same key and attack the companion-device linking handshake performed by installers of this package. The use of CryptoJS symmetric decryption to conceal a single constant in otherwise readable code is a deliberate concealment technique rather than a build artifact, and upstream Baileys does not contain this construct.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
